_link.title: I can describe the roles of the brain and spinal cord as the two components of the central nervous system

toLevel2.stem: What is the role of the brain in the central nervous system?
toLevel2.answer: It coordinates mental processes, behaviour, and bodily activity
distractors: It carries messages between the PNS and skeletal muscles only
It detects stimuli from the external environment and the body
It stores neurochemicals for release into the synaptic cleft

toLevel2.stem: What is the role of the spinal cord in the central nervous system?
toLevel2.answer: It connects the brain to the PNS via afferent and efferent tracts
distractors: It detects stimuli from the environment and sends them to muscles
It produces all neurochemicals used in synaptic transmission
It coordinates mental processes and higher-order thought only

toLevel2.stem: Which two structures make up the central nervous system?
distractors: The brain and peripheral nerves
The spinal cord and sensory neurons
The brain and skeletal muscles

toLevel2.stem: What do afferent tracts in the spinal cord carry?
distractors: Messages away from the brain
Messages between two muscles
Messages within the brain only

toLevel2.stem: What do efferent tracts in the spinal cord carry?
distractors: Messages toward the brain
Messages between two organs
Messages within the cord only

toLevel2.stem: The spinal cord contains afferent tracts that carry messages toward the brain and efferent tracts that carry messages away from the brain.
distractors: False

toLevel2.stem: The spinal cord coordinates mental processes, behaviour, and bodily activity.
distractors: True

toLevel2.stem: The brain coordinates mental processes, {{blank:1}}, and bodily activity.

distractors: digestion
breathing

toLevel2.stem: The spinal cord connects the brain to the PNS via {{blank:1}} tracts that carry messages toward the brain and {{blank:2}} tracts that carry messages away from the brain.

distractors: efferent
autonomic
afferent
somatic

toLevel2.stem: The two components of the central nervous system are the {{blank:1}} and the spinal cord.

distractors: nerves
muscles

toLevel3.stem: Why is the spinal cord described as a connecting structure between the brain and PNS?
toLevel3.answer: It provides the pathway for messages to travel between them
distractors: It processes all information independently of the brain itself
It detects stimuli from the body and sends them to the muscles
It produces neurochemicals that are used by the brain directly

toLevel3.stem: How do afferent and efferent tracts in the spinal cord support the brain's function?
toLevel3.answer: They carry information to and from the brain for processing
distractors: They process information so the brain does not need to act
They replace the brain's role when it is unable to function
They only carry information during sleep and rest periods

toLevel3.stem: Why is knowing the direction of information flow through the spinal cord important?
toLevel3.answer: It is essential for describing conscious responses and reflexes
distractors: Direction is not assessed in VCE Psychology exams at all
All information flows in the same direction through the cord
Direction only matters for the PNS, not the spinal cord

toLevel3.stem: How does the brain's role differ from the spinal cord's role in the CNS?
toLevel3.answer: The brain processes information; the cord connects the brain to the PNS
distractors: The brain and spinal cord perform exactly the same function always
The spinal cord processes information; the brain connects to the PNS
Neither the brain nor the spinal cord processes any information

toLevel3.stem: When a person decides to pick up a cup, which tracts carry the motor command from the brain?
toLevel3.answer: Efferent tracts carry the command away from the brain
distractors: Afferent tracts carry the command toward the brain only
Both afferent and efferent tracts carry the same command
Neither tract is involved in voluntary motor commands

toLevel3.stem: Why is the spinal cord described as a 'cable of nerve tissue'?
toLevel3.answer: It is a long structure that carries bundled neural pathways
distractors: It is made of muscle tissue rather than neural tissue
It is a short structure located entirely within the brain
It does not contain any neural pathways or nerve fibres

toLevel3.stem: Efferent tracts in the spinal cord carry motor commands from the brain toward the PNS.
distractors: False

toLevel3.stem: The brain's role is to {{blank:1}} information, while the spinal cord's role is to {{blank:2}} the brain to the PNS.

distractors: detect
produce
replace
separate

toLevel3.stem: When picking up a cup, the motor command travels from the brain through {{blank:1}} tracts in the spinal cord to reach the muscles.

distractors: afferent
sensory

toLevel3.stem: Knowing the direction of information flow through the spinal cord is essential for describing {{blank:1}} responses and the spinal reflex.

distractors: chemical
structural

toLevel4.stem: Tom touches a hot surface and feels pain. Which spinal cord tracts carry the sensory message toward his brain?
distractors: Efferent (motor) tracts only
Both tracts simultaneously
Neither tract is involved

toLevel4.stem: After feeling the pain, Tom decides to run his hand under cold water. Which spinal cord tracts carry this motor command?
distractors: Afferent (sensory) tracts
Both tracts simultaneously
Neither tract is involved

toLevel4.stem: A student writes: 'The spinal cord processes all information and makes decisions.' How should this be corrected?
toLevel4.answer: The brain processes information; the spinal cord connects the brain to the PNS
distractors: The statement is correct and needs no correction at all
The spinal cord makes decisions but does not process information
The PNS processes information, not the brain or spinal cord

toLevel4.stem: Ella sees a ball coming toward her and decides to catch it. Which description correctly applies the roles of the brain and spinal cord?
toLevel4.answer: The brain decides to catch; efferent tracts carry the command to arm muscles
distractors: The spinal cord decides to catch; afferent tracts carry the command to the brain
The brain detects the ball; the spinal cord decides on the motor response action
Efferent tracts carry the visual information; afferent tracts produce the movement

toLevel4.stem: A VCE exam question asks: 'Describe the role of the spinal cord in a conscious response.' Which answer would earn full marks?
toLevel4.answer: It carries sensory messages to the brain via afferent tracts and motor commands via efferent tracts
distractors: It makes the conscious decision about how to respond to the detected stimulus
It detects the stimulus and sends the information directly to the skeletal muscles
It produces the neurochemicals needed for the response at the neural synapse

toLevel4.stem: A doctor examines a patient with a spinal cord injury who cannot feel sensations in their legs. Which tracts are most likely damaged?
toLevel4.answer: Afferent (sensory) tracts carrying messages toward the brain
distractors: Efferent (motor) tracts carrying messages away from the brain
Both afferent and efferent tracts are completely undamaged
The brain's processing centres are damaged rather than the cord

toLevel4.stem: Marcus is asked to identify the CNS structures involved when he reads a book. Which answer is correct?
toLevel4.answer: The brain processes the visual information; the spinal cord connects it to the PNS
distractors: Only the spinal cord is involved because reading is an automatic process
Only the PNS is involved because the eyes are peripheral sensory organs
The brain and spinal cord are not involved in reading comprehension at all

toLevel4.stem: When Tom feels pain, the sensory message travels through {{blank:1}} tracts in the spinal cord toward the brain.

distractors: efferent
motor

toLevel4.stem: When Ella decides to catch the ball, the motor command travels from her brain through {{blank:1}} tracts to reach her arm muscles.

distractors: afferent
sensory

toLevel4.stem: A patient who cannot feel sensations in their legs likely has damage to the {{blank:1}} tracts in their spinal cord.

distractors: efferent
motor

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that the spinal cord can function independently of the brain for all responses. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Partially correct; the spinal cord mediates reflexes but conscious responses need the brain
distractors: Fully correct; the spinal cord handles all responses without any brain involvement
Fully incorrect; the spinal cord cannot function at all without the brain's input
Partially correct; the brain handles reflexes but the cord handles conscious responses

toLevel5.stem: Dr Lee argues that the brain and spinal cord serve the same function. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; the brain processes information while the cord connects it to the PNS
distractors: Correct; both structures perform identical processing and connecting functions
Correct; there is no functional difference between the brain and the spinal cord
Incorrect; the spinal cord processes information while the brain connects to the PNS

toLevel5.stem: A student writes that efferent tracts carry sensory messages to the brain. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; efferent tracts carry messages away from the brain, not toward it
distractors: Correct; efferent means carrying messages toward the central nervous system
Correct; both afferent and efferent tracts carry messages toward the brain
Incorrect; efferent tracts do not carry any messages in any direction at all

toLevel5.stem: Emma argues that the spinal cord is not part of the CNS because it is located outside the brain. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; the spinal cord is part of the CNS along with the brain
distractors: Correct; only the brain is classified as part of the central nervous system
Correct; the spinal cord belongs to the peripheral nervous system division
Incorrect; the spinal cord is actually located inside the brain structure

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that the brain does not need the spinal cord because it can send signals directly to muscles. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; the spinal cord provides the pathway connecting the brain to the PNS
distractors: Correct; the brain connects directly to all muscles without using the cord
Correct; the spinal cord is unnecessary because the PNS bypasses it entirely
Incorrect; the brain sends signals to the spinal cord but not to any muscles

toLevel5.stem: Marcus argues that afferent and efferent are interchangeable terms for spinal cord tracts. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; afferent means toward the brain and efferent means away from it
distractors: Correct; both terms describe the same direction of information flow always
Correct; the terms have no specific directional meaning in neuroscience
Incorrect; afferent means away from the brain and efferent means toward it

toLevel5.stem: A student suggests that if the spinal cord is damaged, the brain could still control all body movements normally. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; spinal cord damage disrupts the pathway between the brain and PNS
distractors: Correct; the brain has alternative pathways that bypass the spinal cord entirely
Correct; body movements do not require any spinal cord involvement at all
Incorrect; the spinal cord only carries sensory information and not motor commands

toLevel5.stem: A textbook states that the spinal cord 'thinks independently.' Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Misleading; the spinal cord mediates reflexes but does not engage in thought
distractors: Correct; the spinal cord is capable of independent thought and decision-making
Correct; reflexes are a form of thinking that occurs within the spinal cord
Misleading; but only because the spinal cord has no role in any reflexes at all

toLevel5.stem: The claim that the spinal cord can handle all responses independently is {{blank:1}} because conscious responses require processing by the {{blank:2}}.

distractors: fully correct
entirely wrong
muscles
nerves

toLevel5.stem: The claim that efferent tracts carry sensory messages to the brain is {{blank:1}} because efferent tracts carry messages {{blank:2}} the brain.

distractors: correct
plausible
toward
within
